record.context_brief: Groups whose factors differ from L(F_2) model-theoretically
record.original_question: Does there exist an icc non-inner-amenable discrete group G such that its group von Neumann algebra L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to the free group factor L(F_2)?

evidence.quote: Problem 17. Does there exist an icc non inner amenable group G such that L(G) is not elementarily equivalent to L(F2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. A countable discrete group $G$ is said to have infinite conjugacy classes (icc) if every nontrivial element of $G$ has an infinite conjugacy class; equivalently, the group von Neumann algebra $L(G)$ is a $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor. Recall that $L(G)$ is the von Neumann algebra generated by the left regular representation $\lambda:G\to B(\ell^2(G))$, equipped with its canonical faithful normal trace $\tau(x)=\langle x\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle$.

A countable icc group $G$ is called inner amenable if there exists a finitely additive probability measure $m$ on $G\setminus\{e\}$ that is invariant under conjugation by every element of $G$. Otherwise, $G$ is said to be non-inner-amenable.

Two tracial von Neumann algebras $(M_1,\tau_1)$ and $(M_2,\tau_2)$ are elementarily equivalent (in the continuous first-order language of tracial von Neumann algebras) if they satisfy the same first-order sentences; equivalently, they have isomorphic ultrapowers $M_1^{\mathcal U}\cong M_2^{\mathcal U}$ for some (equivalently, every) free ultrafilter $\mathcal U$ on a sufficiently large index set.

Let $\mathbb{F}_2$ denote the free group on two generators, and let $L(\mathbb{F}_2)$ be the associated free group factor.

Question. Does there exist a countable icc non-inner-amenable discrete group $G$ such that the $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $L(G)$ is not elementarily equivalent to $L(\mathbb{F}_2)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in a recent compilation of open problems on ultraproduct II_1 factors. Related results in the literature (e.g., examples of elementarily equivalent groups whose group von Neumann algebras differ, and constructions of inner amenable groups whose L(G) does not have property Gamma) address adjacent questions but do not resolve this one. No published resolution was located.
